title: Check your understanding: Using Revision References

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of using revision references?
options: Revision expressions such as HEAD~1 and HEAD^ follow commit ancestry, while branch and tag names resolve references. Check the history graph first so you know which parent or range the expression selects.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Revision expressions such as HEAD~1 and HEAD^ follow commit ancestry, while branch and tag names resolve references. Check the history graph first so you know which parent or range the expression selects.
questions.explanation: Revision expressions such as HEAD~1 and HEAD^ follow commit ancestry, while branch and tag names resolve references. Check the history graph first so you know which parent or range the expression selects.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git show HEAD~1` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with using revision references?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
